question: Right time to leave, yes or no?

lines.text: The US military says its last troops have now left Iraq.
The final forces left an air base in Erbil, in the Kurdish north.
lines.note: AP: final forces left an air base in Irbil, Kurdish region

lines.text: It ends a twelve-year mission against the Islamic State group.
The Pentagon says the campaign defeated ISIS as an organised military threat.

scene.quote: defeated ISIS as an organized military threat

lines.text: Iraq's prime minister calls it a new phase, defined by Iraq's sovereignty.

scene.quote: a new phase, one defined by Iraq's sovereignty

lines.text: The US invaded in 2003, left in 2011, and returned in 2014 to fight ISIS.
In 2024, Washington and Baghdad agreed to end the mission.
Earlier this year, US forces left Ain al-Asad air base in the west.
lines.note: Reuters via Yahoo; Wikipedia: completed 20 Jan 2026

lines.text: That left hundreds of US troops in the Kurdish north, until now.
lines.note: AP: hundreds of troops in Kurdish region; Reuters: Harir Air Base, Erbil

lines.text: Kurdish officials say the region faced over a thousand drone and missile attacks in the Iran war.
lines.note: AP: more than 1,000 drone and ballistic-missile attacks

lines.text: The Peshmerga ministry says leaving without a defence system is a matter of concern.

scene.quote: without the provision of a defense system, is a matter of concern

lines.text: Powerful Iran-backed groups remain armed. Their disarmament deadline is now June 2027.
lines.note: AP: al-Zaidi delayed militia disarmament deadline to June 2027

lines.text: Twenty-three years after the invasion, the troops are gone. Right time to leave, yes or no?
